target.title: feat(skills): capture reusable techniques from successful work
target.body:
Closes #105672

## What Problem This Solves

Opt-in Skill Workshop autonomy captures explicit corrections, but it loses durable procedures discovered during successful complex work when the user did not phrase the result as a correction.

## Why This Change Was Made

When autonomous capture is enabled, the active agent now reviews successful nontrivial work before its final reply and proposes a reusable technique only when warranted. It prefers revising or updating writable workspace skills, keeps every result pending for review, adds no second model pass or new configuration, and rejects recognized literal credentials before proposal state is written.

## User Impact

Users who enable autonomous Skill Workshop capture can retain useful procedures from successful work without asking explicitly. Routine work, one-offs, user-specific facts, transient failures, unsupported negative claims, and secrets are excluded; defaults and approval boundaries remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxbz7qjc6vdfn1arbdk6j2dp`: 83 focused tests passed across the workshop tool, proposal service, and security scanner.
- Blacksmith Testbox [run 29207215281](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29207215281): `pnpm check:changed` passed on rebased head `f00769fe6da` (core, core tests, docs).
- Live OpenAI `gpt-5.6` eval on public-network AWS Crabbox run `run_f37bc3a92b81`: durable technique updated the relevant skill; routine answer and transient infrastructure failure both abstained.
- Fresh autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
